submission.justification: Recommend Radiator-R2 at 2.7 cm. R1 has the largest raw simulated separation (~4.6 sigma near 2--3 cm) but is an unprotected porous radiator and therefore is not an acceptable choice against the hard humidity-ageing requirement. R2 is the candidate with the documented hydrophobic treatment, so it is the best humidity-qualified option; R3 is solid/lower-index but its simulated separation is substantially lower (~2.9 sigma near 3 cm). A thickness scan of R2 from 1 to 6 cm shows a broad maximum around 2.4--3.0 cm; repeated 100k-event simulations near the maximum gave about 3.9--4.0 sigma at 2.7 cm, while thicker R2 tiles lose performance (e.g. ~3.5 sigma at 5 cm, ~2.8 sigma at 6 cm).

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c.
requirements.evidence: Among humidity-qualified choices, Radiator-R2 outperforms R3. R2 scan: 1 cm 3.36 sigma, 2.4 cm 3.83 sigma, 2.6 cm repeated values 3.74--4.03 sigma, 2.7 cm repeated values 3.876, 3.965, 4.008 sigma, 2.8 cm about 3.67--3.83 sigma, 5 cm 3.46 sigma, 6 cm 2.78 sigma. R3 peaks only around 2.90 sigma at 3 cm. R1 raw separation is higher but excluded by the humidity constraint.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md lists Radiator-R2 as one of the three candidate radiators: a porous radiator with a hydrophobic treatment.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after a 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%.
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R2 is the candidate explicitly specified with a hydrophobic treatment in candidate_specs.md; this is the documented humidity-protection feature. The unprotected porous R1 was excluded despite higher raw separation because the radiator cannot be replaced during the run.
Recommended thickness is 2.7 cm, which lies within the allowed 1--6 cm range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended radiator and thickness.
